experiment: Controlled Intervention 5 - distinguish live-telemetry acquisition from generic missing evidence (single Investigator triage-prompt change)
accepted_stack_before_i5: evaluator mechanism_state auditability (now incl. observed triage choices, 51179e5)
arc03_root_cause: The triage model set needs_live_telemetry=True as a generic 'I need more information' signal. Because telemetry was selected, the no-backend telemetry path ran, tool_failed=True, retrieval never occurred, and the policy produced ESCALATE(tool_failure): the broad decision was accidentally ESCALATE while the evidence path and the escalation reason were both wrong.
hypothesis: If the triage prompt explicitly distinguishes genuine live-telemetry acquisition from generic missing information, document retrieval, and technician-only field inspection, then ARC-03 will stop requesting live telemetry, perform the required Northwind retrieval, and reach ESCALATE(evidence_unresolvable), while ARC-06 keeps requesting telemetry and reaching ESCALATE(tool_failure).
intervention: _TRIAGE_SYSTEM only: needs_live_telemetry set true only when the next step specifically requires obtaining a current machine reading/measurement/status/telemetry value through the live telemetry tool; not a generic uncertainty flag; prefer needs_retrieval when the manual/history corpus is the better source; do not request telemetry when the remaining uncertainty ultimately needs a technician/expert/physical-or-field inspection/unavailable reference instrument; the two flags name the evidence source required next, not the amount of uncertainty. Semantic and general: no ARC references, no fault-type rule, no document IDs, no gold labels, no retrieval-over-telemetry priority.

arc03_target_result.DOC-COMMS-A31_retrieved: 5/5 (plus one non-distractor second hit: DOC-RTU-A11 x4, DOC-FILT-A41 x1)
arc03_target_result.interpretation: The telemetry misclassification is completely and stably fixed: ARC-03 no longer requests telemetry, retrieves DOC-COMMS-A31, and does not hit tool_failure. But the full gold path is not reached: a separate downstream state, the Investigator judging the retrieved manual evidence sufficient (evidence_sufficient=True), drives Diagnosis to answer, so the decision is ANSWER rather than ESCALATE(evidence_unresolvable). This is the evidence-sufficiency cluster (ARC-21), explicitly out of scope for I5.

arc06_contrast_result.interpretation: Contrast preserved: the deliberate telemetry-tool-failure case still requests telemetry and escalates on tool_failure. The intervention did NOT globally suppress telemetry.

cases_requesting_telemetry_under_i5.ARC-02: True 5/5 -> tool_failure 5/5 (gold ASK; pre-existing non-target miss; ARC-02 telemetry behavior is historically variable; NOT newly suppressed by I5 and NOT the target)
cases_requesting_telemetry_under_i5.ARC-06: True 5/5 -> tool_failure 5/5 (gold contrast; correct and preserved)

telemetry_regression_surface.telemetry_removed: ARC-03 only: telemetry 5/5 (pre-I5) -> 0/5 (now retrieves). This is the intended effect.
telemetry_regression_surface.new_tool_failure_introduced: none (only ARC-02/ARC-06 tool-fail, both pre-existing telemetry cases)
telemetry_regression_surface.arc08_note: ARC-08 fails retrieval-behavior/source under I5 (no_retrieval vs gold 'required'), but this is PRE-EXISTING in the accepted stack: I2 ran no_retrieval 5/5 with ESCALATE(conflict_unresolvable) 5/5. ARC-08 decision+reason remain correct 5/5 under I5. Not an I5 regression; it only looks new relative to Baseline v1 (which retrieved).
telemetry_regression_surface.arc18_note: ARC-18 over-retrieval remains failing (known cluster, out of scope).

decision_correct.note: pre-I5 accepted (I2) decision mean 16.0; ARC-03 decision flips from accidentally-correct ESCALATE(tool_failure) to ANSWER, so ARC-03 decision_correct goes pass->fail; net flat-to-slightly-down, within run-to-run spread.

dimension_note: Movements off ARC-03/06 (grounding 4-7, structured 18-20, a one-off ARC-01/ARC-14 miss) are unrelated Diagnosis/grounding stochasticity, not attributable to the triage-prompt change; reported descriptively, no composite score, no significance claim (n=5).
verdict: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The telemetry classification is fixed exactly as hypothesized and with unusual stability: ARC-03 needs_live_telemetry=False 5/5 (was telemetry 5/5), retrieves DOC-COMMS-A31 5/5, tool_failed eliminated 5/5; ARC-06 preserved 5/5 (telemetry + tool_failure); no legitimate telemetry path suppressed and no new tool_failure introduced. BUT the ARC-03 decision/reason target is not met: evidence_sufficient=True 5/5 drives ANSWER 5/5 instead of ESCALATE(evidence_unresolvable). The remaining miss is the separate, out-of-scope evidence-sufficiency cluster (ARC-21), not a telemetry problem. Not HARMFUL (ARC-06 intact, no material regressions).
retain_or_revert_recommendation: RETAIN as a correctness fix, with an explicit caveat and deferring to Ken. Rationale: the change corrects a genuine evidence-path bug (telemetry was being used as a generic uncertainty flag), the evidence path is now correct and well-motivated, ARC-06 is preserved, and there are no harmful regressions, mirroring the reasoning by which Intervention 2 was retained despite a flat decision score. Caveat to weigh: unlike I2, I5 flips ARC-03's headline decision from accidentally-correct ESCALATE(tool_failure) to ANSWER (wrong), so decision_correct on ARC-03 regresses pass->fail and the overall decision mean is flat-to-slightly-down (15.6 vs 16.0). The full ARC-03 gold path requires separately fixing the downstream evidence-sufficiency misjudgment (ARC-21 cluster). No second behavioral change made; retain/revert is Ken's call.
remaining_untouched_clusters: ARC-21 evidence sufficiency (now the ARC-03 blocker)
codex_prerun_review: PASS (one triage-prompt intervention narrowing needs_live_telemetry; no global telemetry suppression; nothing else in the behavioral path changed).
